# Generated files

Drizzle snapshots are maintained in the format supported by the installed Drizzle Kit. After a Kit upgrade, use `pnpm --filter @blossom/app exec drizzle-kit up` to upgrade old snapshots; do not edit historical migration SQL. Check that generation reports no unexpected schema changes and test migrations against a disposable database.

Do not hand-edit a generated file: the next run overwrites the edit or leaves the output out of step with its source. Change the source, run the generator, and review the result. "Tracked" means committed to git (checked against the git index and `.gitignore`).

| Output                                                    | Tracked | Source                                                | Generated by                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app/src/route-tree.gen.ts`                               | yes     | route files under `app/src/routes/`                   | TanStack Start's router plugin during `vite dev` / `vite build`                                    |
| `app/src/paraglide/`                                      | no      | `app/messages/*.json`, `app/project.inlang/`          | Paraglide Vite plugin during `vite dev` / `vite build`; `paraglide-js compile` in `pnpm test`      |
| `app/drizzle/<timestamp>_<name>/{migration.sql,snapshot.json}` | yes | `app/src/db/*-schema.ts`                          | `pnpm --filter @blossom/app db:generate`                                                           |
| `server-agent/openapi/spec.json`                          | yes     | the app's agent oRPC router and zod schemas           | `pnpm --filter @blossom/app agent:spec` (needs the dev server running)                             |
| `server-agent/openapi/spec-3.1.json`                      | no      | same                                                  | intermediate step of `agent:spec`                                                                  |
| progenitor client (`OUT_DIR/codegen.rs`)                  | no      | `server-agent/openapi/spec.json`                      | `server-agent/build.rs` on `cargo build` / `cargo test`                                            |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `server-agent/Cargo.lock`               | yes     | package manifests                                     | `pnpm install`, `cargo` (CI uses `--frozen-lockfile` and `--locked`)                               |
| `app/dist/`, `app/.output/`, `.vercel/`, `.netlify/`, `.wrangler/`, `.tanstack/`, `.nitro/`, `server-agent/target/` | no | build tooling | `vite build`, wrangler, cargo                                              |

## Route tree

`app/src/route-tree.gen.ts` is regenerated whenever the dev server or a build runs. It is committed, so after adding, renaming or deleting a route file, run `pnpm dev` (or `pnpm build`) and commit the updated file with the route change. Its header disables oxlint and type checking, and `.oxfmtrc.json` ignores `*.gen.*`, so the formatter will not touch it. Route files under `_modules/` are ignored by the router on purpose. `app/tsr.config.json` configures the standalone `tsr` CLI (installed as a dev dependency); the normal workflow does not need it.

## Translations

Edit `app/messages/en.json` and `app/messages/zh-cn.json`, never `app/src/paraglide/` (git-ignored by its own `.gitignore`). The app's `test` script recompiles Paraglide before running Vitest, so the generated messages exist even on a clean checkout; running `vitest` directly skips that step and relies on a previously generated directory. The inlang plugin modules are referenced by CDN URL in `app/project.inlang/settings.json`, so a first compile may need network access or a warm `project.inlang/cache` (offline behaviour not verified).

## Database migrations

Generate with `db:generate`, review `migration.sql`, and commit the new folder (both files) together with the schema change. `snapshot.json` is Drizzle Kit's record of the schema after that migration; do not edit it by hand, and do not modify a migration that has been applied. Applying migrations (`db:migrate`) is a separate step that changes whatever database `DATABASE_URL` points at; see [API, data and auth](api-data-auth.md#migrations) for what each Drizzle command does and how to verify against a disposable database.

## Agent OpenAPI spec and client

The agent's Rust client is generated from the app's API, so the order matters:

1. Change the agent procedures or schemas under `app/src/orpc/` (and keep `agent-v3.test.ts` current).
2. Start the dev server (`pnpm dev`, <http://localhost:3000>). It is a long-running process and needs the server environment to validate (at least `DATABASE_URL` and `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, normally from `app/.env.local`). If you supply values yourself, point `DATABASE_URL` at a disposable database. Whether generating the spec actually connects to the database is not verified here. Stop the server when you are done.
3. In another shell: `pnpm --filter @blossom/app agent:spec`. It downloads `/api/spec.json` to `server-agent/openapi/spec-3.1.json`, then `openapi-down-convert` writes the OpenAPI 3.0 `server-agent/openapi/spec.json`.
4. Commit `spec.json` (the 3.1 intermediate is ignored). Review its diff: it should contain only the changes you intended.
5. In `server-agent/`, `cargo test --locked` (or `cargo build`); `build.rs` regenerates the client from `spec.json` and reruns when it changes.

If you cannot run the dev server, say so in your report and leave the spec untouched rather than editing `spec.json` by hand; a stale spec would make the agent build against an outdated contract.

## Lockfiles

Change dependencies with `pnpm add`/`pnpm remove` (from `app/` or with `--filter @blossom/app`; root dev tools at the root) or `cargo add`, which update the lockfile. Do not edit lockfiles manually. Keep unrelated lockfile churn out of a change; a large unexplained lockfile diff means something other than the intended dependency moved. Renovate (`renovate.json`) also proposes upgrades.

## Local and build artefacts

`app/.env.local` and other `*.local` files are ignored by git and may hold real secrets: keep their values out of output, docs, tests and commits. Build output and tool caches in the table above are ignored too; they should not be staged.
